title: Must-read fallback contract hardening
summary: Project iteration record for preventing sparse main_items reports from reaching page-check without exactly three reader-facing must-read cards when other public sourced sections can fill the surface.

lessons.lesson: Report-write validation must evaluate the same public reference pool that the renderer and page-check expect.
lessons.evidence: The blocked daily run had fewer than three main_items but enough public sourced sections for must-read fallback, so a main_items-only validation bypass let an invalid public surface proceed.
lessons.recommended_action: Keep hero_highlights enforcement tied to eligible public reference items rather than only main_items count.

suggestions.issue: A sparse report could pass report-write with only two hero_highlights when the third public reference lived outside main_items.
suggestions.evidence: The new regression test fails without the report-write contract change and passes once eligible public reference items trigger the exactly-three hero_highlights requirement.
suggestions.suggestion: Require exactly three hero_highlights whenever at least three public reference items with title and URL are available across all rendered daily sections.
suggestions.expected_benefit: The daily runner blocks early with a repairable data contract error instead of producing a page that fails visual page-check after build.
suggestions.promotion_path: Implemented in report-write normalization and covered by unit tests plus the full repository validation gate.
validation_evidence: report write requires must read backfill when public references can fill three cards
report:draft backfills must read highlights from public sections when main items are sparse
interaction input puts must read first and compact main list

followups.action: Run the fixed Codex-native daily publish flow from latest main after the PR is merged.
